name: Referral Intake & Thank-You Loop

parameters.content:
## Referral Intake & Thank-You Loop

### How it works

This workflow has TWO independent triggers on one canvas:

**A. Referral intake (top row)**
1. Fires on any web form submission that identifies a referrer (Fluent Forms, or any generic JSON/form-encoded POST) — same dual-format normalization pattern as PAC-32's Lead-Source ROI Tracker. A submission with no referrer name at all isn't a referral and this workflow drops it immediately.
2. Logs the referral to a Google Sheets ledger — the permanent, human-reviewable record of who referred whom and when.
3. If the referrer left an email address, thanks them personally through the compliance guardrail (so an opt-out is respected, and the send is logged) — a short, warm note that never mentions the lead's legal matter or practice area, since that's not the referrer's information to know.
4. Always emails the firm a summary of the new referral, regardless of whether a thank-you could be sent.

**B. Monthly reciprocal-referral reminder (bottom row) — a second, independent branch**
Runs once a month, re-reads the entire ledger, and surfaces every referrer who's sent 2 or more referrals in the trailing 90 days. This is a business-development nudge only — it never decides who to refer back to or drafts anything on the firm's behalf; it just makes sure a generous referral source doesn't go unnoticed and unreciprocated.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Set up the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) first — the referrer thank-you goes through it.
- [ ] Create a Google Sheet with a 'Referrals' tab and columns: date, lead_name, lead_email, referrer_name, referrer_email, referrer_type, matter_type, status.
- [ ] Configure Google Sheets OAuth2 and SMTP credentials.
- [ ] Set the required n8n Variables: FIRM_NAME, FIRM_EMAIL, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID, REFERRAL_LEDGER_SHEET_ID.
- [ ] Add a 'Referred by' (name) and optional 'Referred by email' field to your intake form, and point its webhook feed at this workflow's Production URL.
- [ ] Activate the workflow.

### Customization

Edit the wording in 'Build Referral Thank You Email' and 'Build Reciprocal Referral Reminder Email' to match your firm's voice. The reciprocity threshold (2 referrals in 90 days) is set at the top of 'Compute Referral Counts By Referrer' if you want it more or less sensitive.

## Receive and validate the referral

Accepts a submission from Fluent Forms or any generic JSON/form-encoded POST, trusting only that a referrer name was provided. Anything without one is dropped — this workflow has nothing to do with a non-referred lead.

## Log to the ledger, then thank the referrer

Every valid referral is appended to the Google Sheets ledger first, unconditionally. The referrer only gets thanked if they left an email address and haven't opted out — the ledger entry happens either way.

## Notify the firm

Always fires, regardless of which thank-you path was taken above — the firm gets a summary of every new referral either way.

## Monthly reciprocal-referral reminder — a second, independent branch

Runs on its own schedule, completely separate from the intake branch above. Re-reads the whole ledger and surfaces any referrer who's sent 2+ referrals in the last 90 days — a business-development nudge, not an automated action. Never fires if nobody qualifies.

nodes.name: When Referral Form Is Submitted
nodes.notes:
Receives a referral-intake submission — one URL handles any connected source. Paste the Production URL (visible after activating this workflow) into your intake form's webhook/notification settings (e.g. Fluent Forms → Form Settings → Notifications → Webhooks). Add a 'Referred by' field (and ideally 'Referred by email') to that form so this workflow has something to act on.

Responds immediately (default response mode) so the form's webhook delivery doesn't time out waiting for the compliance check and email sends to finish.

This is a generic form webhook, not a Clio API webhook — no OAuth scope, no verification handshake, no expiring subscription to maintain (unlike PAC-66's Clio-webhook design). Much simpler because the caller here is a form tool you configure directly, not a third-party API requiring registration.

nodes.name: Normalize Referral Submission
nodes.notes: Extracts lead and referrer details from whichever form field names arrived. is_valid_referral is false when no referrer name was found anywhere in the payload — the next node routes that to a labelled Skip rather than logging a non-referral to the ledger.

nodes.name: If Valid Referral Submission
nodes.notes:
Yes (a referrer name was found) → log it to the ledger and consider a thank-you.
No (no referrer info at all — a normal, non-referred lead) → route to Skip. Nothing is logged.

nodes.name: Skip — Not A Referral
nodes.notes: This submission didn't identify a referrer — nothing for this template to track. Your normal intake process (e.g. PAC-20's Clio Intake Sync) still handles the lead itself; this workflow is referral-specific.

nodes.name: Log Referral To Ledger
nodes.notes:
Appends one row per referral — the permanent, human-reviewable record this template exists to build. Written unconditionally, before any thank-you attempt, so a referral is captured even if the referrer left no email and can't be thanked directly.

REFERRAL_LEDGER_SHEET_ID is the Google Sheet's ID (the long string in its URL between /d/ and /edit). Create the sheet first with a 'Referrals' tab and these column headers: date, lead_name, lead_email, referrer_name, referrer_email, referrer_type, matter_type, status.

Does not deduplicate — the same referrer submitting twice logs twice. Review the sheet periodically, or ask Protomated about the done-for-you dedupe upgrade.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → Google Sheets OAuth2 → sign in with the account that owns this sheet.

nodes.name: If Referrer Has Email
nodes.notes:
Yes (referrer left an email) → check compliance, then thank them personally.
No (name only, e.g. 'a friend told them') → route to Skip. The referral is still logged in the ledger above; there's just no address to send a thank-you to.

nodes.name: Skip — No Referrer Email On File
nodes.notes: The referrer's name is logged in the ledger, but no email address was captured, so there's no way to send a personal thank-you. The firm still gets notified of this referral next.

nodes.name: Build Referral Thank You Email
nodes.notes: Plain-text, deliberately light content — no case details, no practice area, nothing that could reveal anything about why the referred lead is seeking legal help. Just gratitude.

nodes.name: Check Compliance Before Thanking Referrer
nodes.notes:
Checks whether this referrer has opted out of firm emails — a referrer is a real contact receiving an automated firm communication, so the same opt-out respect applies as any other outbound message. Appends the required unsubscribe footer and logs the attempt to the audit sheet.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable. This REPLACES $json with the guardrail's own response, so 'Send Referral Thank You Email' reaches back to 'Build Referral Thank You Email' by name for the subject line (confirmed pattern from PAC-65/66/67 — reading $json.subject here would be blank).

nodes.name: If Thank You Approved
nodes.notes:
Yes (referrer hasn't opted out) → send the thank-you.
No (opted out) → route to Skip. The suppression is already logged by the guardrail.

nodes.name: Send Referral Thank You Email
nodes.notes:
Sends the compliance-approved thank-you — the plain-text body (message_out from the guardrail, carrying the required unsubscribe footer). Subject reaches back to 'Build Referral Thank You Email' by name since the guardrail call replaced $json.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

nodes.name: Skip — Referrer Opted Out
nodes.notes: This referrer has opted out of firm emails. The suppression is already logged by the guardrail workflow. The referral is still in the ledger, and the firm still gets notified next.

nodes.name: Build Firm Referral Notification
nodes.notes: Converges here from all three possible thank-you outcomes (sent, opted out, no email) — same convergence pattern as PAC-32's Build Firm Alert. Always fires exactly once per referral.

nodes.name: Send Firm Referral Notification
nodes.notes: Emails the firm a summary of every new referral, whatever the thank-you outcome was. Same SMTP credential as the thank-you email — no separate setup.

nodes.name: Send Reciprocal Referral Reminder Monthly
nodes.notes: Fires on the 1st of every month at 8am (n8n server timezone) — adjust the cron expression if a different day/time suits your firm. Completely independent of the intake branch above; reads the whole ledger fresh every time rather than tracking anything incrementally.

nodes.name: Read Referral Ledger
nodes.notes:
Reads every row ever logged to the same 'Referrals' sheet the intake branch appends to. Returns one n8n item per row, with each column as a field.

Not yet independently confirmed live: whether Google Sheets returns the 'date' column back as the exact ISO string it was written as, or reformats it (e.g. to a locale date string) depending on the column's cell format. Check this node's raw output on your first real run — if dates come back reformatted, 'Compute Referral Counts By Referrer' downstream may need its date parsing adjusted.

Credential: same Google Sheets OAuth2 credential as the ledger-logging step above.

nodes.name: Compute Referral Counts By Referrer
nodes.notes: Correctly left in default 'Run Once for All Items' mode — this node genuinely needs every ledger row together to compute a count per referrer, unlike the per-item Compute nodes in PAC-67 which each handle one record independently.

nodes.name: Filter Referrers Needing A Reciprocity Nudge
nodes.notes: Keeps only referrers with 2 or more referrals in the trailing 90 days — adjust the threshold in this condition if your firm wants a more or less sensitive nudge. On most months this drops to zero, which is normal, not a failure.

nodes.name: Aggregate Referrers For Reminder
nodes.notes: Standard n8n core node — collapses every qualifying referrer into a single item's 'referrers' array so the next step builds one digest email instead of one per referrer.

nodes.name: Build Reciprocal Referral Reminder Email
nodes.notes: Correctly left in default 'Run Once for All Items' mode — this node genuinely only ever receives ONE item, the aggregated array from 'Aggregate Referrers For Reminder'.

nodes.name: Log Reminder For Compliance Audit
nodes.notes:
Logs the reminder send to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet — internal record-keeping only, this goes to the firm, not a client or the referrer. Its 'approved'/opt-out result is deliberately ignored, same fire-and-forget pattern used for internal-only notifications elsewhere in this catalog (PAC-59/60/61/63/67).

This REPLACES $json with the guardrail's own response, so 'Send Reciprocal Referral Reminder Email' reaches back to 'Build Reciprocal Referral Reminder Email' by name for every field it needs.

nodes.name: Send Reciprocal Referral Reminder Email
nodes.notes:
Delivers the monthly digest to FIRM_EMAIL. Reads every field explicitly from 'Build Reciprocal Referral Reminder Email' by name rather than $json, since the guardrail call immediately upstream replaced the item's json with its own response.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

main.node: Skip — No Referrer Email On File
Filter Referrers Needing A Reciprocity Nudge

description: Runs on two independent triggers. Intake: fires on a referral-tagged form submission, logs it unconditionally to a Google Sheets ledger, thanks the referrer through the Bar-Compliance Guardrail if they left an email (never mentioning the lead's legal matter), and always emails the firm a summary. Monthly: a completely independent rollup re-reads the whole ledger and surfaces any referrer who's sent 2 or more referrals in the trailing 90 days, as a business-development nudge to reciprocate — never an automated action. Replaces Lawmatics referral management. A missed or unthanked referral source is a leak that quietly dries up over time.
